skill.name: slb
skill.description: Adds a Simultaneous Launch Button workflow that requires peer review before AI agents run destructive shell commands.
skill.summary: Require second approval before dangerous agent commands execute.
skill.author: Dicklesworthstone

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by markdown examples of shell commands that SLB is designed to classify and guard. Real risks remain in the curl-to-bash installer, hidden Claude hook configuration write, inherited cloud credentials, broad TCP binding example, local socket handling, command-history database, and documented bypass modes.

remediation.suggestion: Replace the curl-to-bash one-liner with verified release downloads, checksum verification, or go install as the primary path.
Require explicit user confirmation and show a diff before writing ~/.claude/hooks.json or other agent configuration files.
Document least-privilege profiles and provide options to scrub or allowlist environment variables during execution.

remediation.issue: Remote daemon TCP example binds to all interfaces
remediation.suggestion: Prefer localhost binding in examples and require authentication plus narrow allowlists for remote mode.
Make bypass features opt-in, auditable, and clearly marked as weakening the two-person rule.

semantic_findings.title: Powerful Emergency Override Can Bypass Peer Review
semantic_findings.description: The skill documents an emergency-execute mode that allows a human to bypass the approval workflow with logging and hash acknowledgment. This may be valid for incidents, but it weakens the advertised two-person rule if enabled without strict policy controls.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The emergency override section explicitly describes bypassing normal approval for command execution. The safeguards reduce risk, but the bypass is a real policy-sensitive capability.

semantic_findings.title: Trusted Self-Approval Weakens Separation of Duties
semantic_findings.description: The example configuration supports trusted_self_approve agents. This can undermine the two-person approval model if trusted agents are compromised or misconfigured.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The configuration example directly names trusted_self_approve and a delay. The feature may be intentional, but it creates a clear separation-of-duties exception.

content.user_title: Require Peer Approval for Risky Agent Commands
content.value_statement: AI coding agents can run destructive commands too quickly in shared projects. SLB adds a peer review gate before high-risk shell actions execute.
actual_capabilities: Classifies shell commands into safe, caution, dangerous, and critical risk tiers.
Requires one or more approvals before dangerous or critical commands execute.
Binds approvals to command hashes to detect tampering before execution.
Tracks sessions, pending requests, reviews, outcomes, and history.
Provides Claude Code hook integration for pre-tool-use command checks.
Supports daemon, TUI, watch stream, rollback capture, and dry-run workflows.
limitations: It does not replace least-privilege credentials, backups, or environment isolation.
Client-side execution means approved commands inherit the user shell environment.
Emergency override and trusted self-approval can weaken peer review guarantees.
Safe operation depends on correct pattern configuration and reviewer judgment.

use_cases.title: Guard destructive agent actions
use_cases.description: Require another reviewer before agents run commands such as force push, database drops, or recursive deletion.

use_cases.title: Add audit trails to multi-agent work
use_cases.description: Record command requests, reasons, approvals, rejections, outcomes, and execution history for later review.

use_cases.title: Integrate command gates into Claude Code
use_cases.description: Install a pre-tool-use hook that classifies shell commands and blocks risky actions until reviewed.

prompt_templates.title: Start a protected session
prompt_templates.scenario: Begin using SLB in a project.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me initialize SLB for this repository and start a named agent session.

prompt_templates.title: Request approval for a risky command
prompt_templates.scenario: Run a command only after review.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an SLB request for this command with a clear reason and show what reviewers should check.

prompt_templates.title: Review a pending command
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the pending SLB request, explain the risks, and recommend approve or reject.

prompt_templates.title: Design a safer approval policy
prompt_templates.scenario: Customize SLB for a team workflow.
prompt_templates.prompt: Propose SLB risk tiers, approval counts, timeout behavior, and hook settings for our multi-agent development workflow.

output_examples.input: Request approval to clean build artifacts.
output: A pending request is created for the cleanup command.
The request includes the command, reason, risk tier, requester session, and required approvals.
The review highlights branch rewrite risk and asks for confirmation of the target branch.
The reviewer can approve with a comment or reject with a reason.
A history view summarizes executed, rejected, timed out, and failed requests.
Outcome notes help tune future risk patterns.

best_practices: Use least-privilege credentials before running commands through SLB.
Require different reviewers for dangerous and critical commands.
Review hook and daemon configuration before enabling automation.
anti_patterns: Do not rely on emergency override for routine work.
Do not auto-approve commands that can delete data or rewrite history.
Do not expose the daemon TCP listener without authentication and narrow network access.

faq.question: Does SLB execute commands on a remote server?
faq.answer: No. Commands run in the local shell environment. The daemon verifies approvals and coordinates state.

faq.question: Can it prevent every destructive action?
faq.answer: No. It adds approval gates and audit logs, but users still need backups, permissions, and safe infrastructure controls.

faq.question: Why are command hashes used?
faq.answer: Hashes bind approval to the exact command text. Execution is rejected if the command changes after approval.

faq.question: Does it work with Claude Code?
faq.answer: The skill documents a Claude Code hook integration that can classify shell commands before tool use.

faq.question: What should be reviewed before publishing this skill?
faq.answer: Review the install method, hook writes, TCP mode, credential inheritance, and emergency bypass behavior.

faq.question: Who benefits most from SLB?
faq.answer: Teams running multiple AI agents in repositories, infrastructure projects, or databases where one command can cause major damage.
